Continuing the spherical kernel

Written by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), October 2026. Public domain (CC0).

The spherical representation of a distribution becomes a local tool only after its kernel is understood away from the real boundary point being studied. We prove the kernel's complex continuation, its exponential decrease in separated complex directions, and its exact leading boundary growth. A final localization statement shows why a distribution supported away from a point contributes a holomorphic remainder there.

The kernel and its normalization come from Holomorphic decompositions of tempered distributions, Lemmas 1–2 and Theorems 3–4. We use Boundary flux and weak identities, Theorem 2.1 and Corollaries 2.3–2.4, for divergence and complex Green, including finite corners; Lipschitz graphs and surface measures, Theorem 2.1, for the graph density and its rotation invariance; Cauchy kernels and distributional boundary limits, Corollary 2.2, for disk power series; and Holomorphic boundaries in convex cones, its polydisk Cauchy proof, for derivative estimates. The identity principle is proved in Gluing holomorphic sides, Lemma 3.2. The right-half-plane logarithm and damped Euler integral are Complex powers at a boundary, Lemmas H0–H1. The accompanying gamma proof, Fourier foundation, and integration foundation supply their complete scalar, Gaussian, measure and Fourier normalizations.
